newsitem.title: USA: AMEX sets Centennial options resumption.
newsitem.headline: AMEX sets Centennial options resumption.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange (AMEX) said Wednesday it would resume options trading on shares of Centennial Technologies Inc immediately after the underlying shares re-opened for trade at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
Late Tuesday, the NYSE halted trading in Centennial shares after they had rallied sharply. The halt remained in effect Wednesday. The stock last closed at 14-3/4.
The AMEX also said when Centennial options re-open, trading will be limited to closing transactions.
"The exchange deems this action appropriate in the interest of maintaining a fair and orderly market in CTN options and for the protection of investors," the AMEX said in a statement.
On February 18, the NYSE said it would suspend trading of Centennial common stock on March 3 and would afterwards apply with federal regulators to delist it.
That same day, Centennial said it would restate its results to show losses for fiscal 1996 and the first quarter of 1997 and would revise its second quarter 1997 results to show a loss.
The personal computer card maker boaasted the best-performing share price of 1996 on the NYSE, ending the year at 52 a share.
On February 11, the company fired its chief executive officer Emanuel Pinez and relieved chief financial officer James Murphy of his duties.
The Securities and Exchange Commission later charged Pinez with insider trading, altering inventory and fraud.
